scope: All visitor-facing source-derived language, including headline, explanatory synthesis, cocktail repeats and repeated functions or approval boundaries.
countingMethod: Every factual paraphrase and repetition is charged once to an official source that directly supports it. No factual synthesis is excluded as editorial authority; only the verified Library lesson is separate.

fragments.text: HoneyBook users can now ask ChatGPT about their client work—and approve drafts before anything goes out.
On September 9, HoneyBook announced a plugin that connects its client-management service to ChatGPT.
An existing HoneyBook user can connect her account, then ask ChatGPT about the projects, contracts, invoices and payments stored there.
OpenAI’s official listing says the plugin requires a HoneyBook account.
The useful change is that ChatGPT can answer from the HoneyBook records you allow it to reach.
You could ask which payments are overdue, where a project stands or have a proposal prepared from a saved template.
HoneyBook says anything the plugin builds stays a draft. Nothing sends, changes or reaches a client until you review and approve it.
When connecting, you choose which HoneyBook resources it can reach, and you can disconnect it later in ChatGPT settings without changing your HoneyBook account.
For an existing HoneyBook user, one conversation can move from “what is happening?” to a prepared next step.
The boundary is read, draft, review, approve. The plugin can prepare work from the connected account; you remain the person who decides whether that HoneyBook change or client message happens.
fragments.rationale: Factual synthesis of HoneyBook’s exact account, draft and approval statements; charged rather than exempted as editorial authority.

fragments.text: HoneyBook’s ChatGPT plugin can answer from the account areas you approve and prepare things like proposals or payment requests.
Its work stays in draft until you review and approve it.

AI Fundamentals 101: The Autonomy Spectrum explains “propose, then approve”: a system prepares an action, and an authorised person confirms before it happens. That is the useful pattern in HoneyBook’s stated draft boundary.
fragments.rationale: Verified AI Fundamentals 101 chapter 13.3 destination and propose-then-approve definition.
